synopsis: Lockheed Martin participated with NASA and the US Air Force Research Laboratory in Auto-GCAS research dating to the early 1980s, a history repeated in Chapter 2 and the glossary [f1439, f15733]. Lockheed Martin says F-35 integration occurred in 2019, seven years ahead of the previous plan, thanks to agile development and reuse of F-16 work [f1443]. By that integration milestone, the company credited Auto-GCAS with saving eight F-16 pilots’ lives [f1444]. The facts thus distinguish a long research history from accelerated integration on a later platform; the schedule acceleration and lives-saved count are vendor-attributed claims [f1439, f1443, f1444].

relations.note: Both date joint NASA, AFRL and Lockheed Martin research to the early 1980s.
